findings.reason: the batch instruction is the only dispatch wire the plan carries (no depends-on/informs/gates metas, all section data-links empty), so its omission of §19 and §20 silently drops two implementable sections from the wave.
findings.text: the open driving followup reads "§2–§16 and §18 are independent ... queue them all in one batch", while _document's plan-section-declarations (plan.html:22) declares s19 and s20 implementable; a coordinator following the followup it is given dispatches neither, and both sections sit unbuilt with nothing naming them as deliberately excluded

findings.reason: a node cannot tell whether to copy the brief and fall back, or re-compose and require the reviewed run's record; the two choices implement opposite behaviours and only one matches the deliverable's first sentence.
findings.text: §18's deliverable says a queued request "launches with the brief it was dispatched with, whatever happens to run directories other than its own and, for a composed run review, the reviewed run's", but no case removes the reviewed run's directory and the next sentence says a composed review "may still re-compose its brief at launch from the reviewed run's record", so the deliverable's strongest claim is measured nowhere and is contradicted by the clause beside it; a composed launch that requires the reviewed run's record fails exactly the case the deliverable says must survive

findings.reason: a node implementing "whatever the line holds" removes the unresolvable-sha refusal the section says to preserve, while a node preserving it violates the same paragraph; the endpoint has to say which clause wins, and the done-when's unresolvable-sha case does not state whether --no-commit is present, so the run cannot settle it by measuring.
findings.text: §19's deliverable states "--no-commit with a reason is honoured whatever the manifest's commits line holds" and in the next sentence "A run whose commits line names a sha that does not resolve is still refused as now"; an unresolvable sha is a value the commits line can hold, so the first clause licenses exactly the promotion the second refuses
